request.description: A dungeon wall of cold grey quarried stone, seen straight on from the front. Level courses of blocks, the courses uneven in height and the vertical joints offset irregularly, blocks of different lengths, three or four of them replaced with mismatched salvage stone. The mortar joints are much darker than the block faces, roughly a third of their brightness, and each block carries a single lighter pixel along its top edge. Where a block has been replaced the gap around it is packed with smaller chipped stone in a coarser, paler mortar, so the eye reads old block, new packing, old block. Laid horizontally across the whole width is a squared timber baulk that runs off both the left and right edges and continues past them, standing proud of the stone with a darker under-edge. It is fixed by two driven iron pins, each a small square head with a bitten rim, and the stone around each is bruised dark. One turn of rope is wrapped over the timber where it crosses a joint. The top four rows of the frame are the wall's upper surface: one flat value, clearly lighter than the front face, meeting it on a single hard line. Everything below that is front face, all the way to the bottom of the frame. Stone from edge to edge.
